newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caymans to have ethics code for offshore firms.
newsitem.headline: Caymans to have ethics code for offshore firms.

text.p: The newly-formed Cayman Islands Offshore Co. Managers Association will adopt a code of ethics for its members to work by.
Association President Paul Harris said he believed the code of ethics would be the first of its kind for any offshore financial jurisdiction.
It will specifically address matters that relate to problems and actions confronting the offshore company managment industry.
Among those problems are money-laundering and hiding illegally obtained assets from officials in other jurisdictions.
Tax evasion, however, is not a problem in the Cayman Islands as the jurisdiction has no taxes and does not recognise tax problems or disputes from other countries.
The code will also require offshore company managers to maintain their companies in compliance with Cayman law or face penalties from the association.
Harris also called on non-members of the association who deal in the offshore management industry to adopt the code.

There are at present some 50,000 offshore companies registered in the Cayman Islands, along with 32 companies that are recognised and licensed by government as offshore company managers. Of those 23 are association members, Harris said.
